description: Given a wooden stick of length n and an array of cuts positions. The cost of a cut is the length of the stick being cut. Return the minimum total cost of all cuts. You can change the order of cuts.
intuition: This is interval DP where you try every possible order of cuts. The cost of each cut is the length of the current stick segment. Add endpoints 0 and n, sort, and dp[i][j] represents the minimum cost to make all cuts between positions i and j.
approach: Add 0 and n to the cuts array and sort. Use interval DP where dp[i][j] = minimum cost to make all cuts between cuts[i] and cuts[j]. The cost of a cut is cuts[j] - cuts[i] plus the cost of the two resulting segments.
explanation:
1. Add endpoints 0 and n to cuts and sort them.
2. dp[i][j] = min cost to perform all cuts between cuts[i] and cuts[j].
3. For each interval [i, j], try each cut position k between i and j.
4. Cost of cutting at k = (cuts[j] - cuts[i]) + dp[i][k] + dp[k][j].
5. Take the minimum over all k.
timeComplexity: O(m^3) where m is the number of cuts
hints: Add 0 and n as boundaries. Sort the cuts.
Use interval DP: dp[i][j] is the minimum cost for the segment from cuts[i] to cuts[j].
Try each intermediate cut point and take the minimum.
